entities.name: Marcus Publicius Malleolus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Publicius Malleolus was a Roman statesman who served as Consul in 246 BCE. As part of the Second Punic War, he participated in a naval battle against Carthage off the coast of Sicily.

Malleolus played a key role in the Roman campaign to retake Sardinia from the Carthaginians, contributing significantly to their ultimate victory. His efforts helped pave the way for the Roman expansion into North Africa.

The legacy of Marcus Publicius Malleolus can be seen in the continued Roman dominance of the Mediterranean region. He was one of the last prominent Roman generals to serve under the Republic before its eventual fall to the dictator Julius Caesar.

In 250 BCE, Malleolus died at the age of approximately 80, leaving behind a legacy as one of Rome's most respected Consuls.
